newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus shares up 2.77 pct on cement buying spree.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus shares up 2.77 pct on cement buying spree.

text.p: Speculation of a merger between Cyprus's two cement industries pushed stocks on the Cyprus exchange up 2.77 percent by the end of the week, analysts said on Friday.
Unconfirmed reports of a bid by the Cyprus Cement Company to take over Vassiliko Cement fuelled speculation on the market and drove shares of both companies higher over the past two days.
"We have not been told what is going on and we are seeing a lot of speculative buying," said one broker.

Vassiliko cement closed on its fully paid shares at 170.5 on Friday, gaining 24 percent on last Friday's close of 137.5. Cyprus Cement saw an 11.9 percent rise in its shares, closing on Friday at 243.5.
The bull run started on Wednesday when news broke that Paschalis Paschalides, long-time chairman of the Hellenic Group of Companies which controls Vassiliko, quit.

He cited managerial differences with the Greek Orthodox Church, which in turn controls the Hellenic Group. Media reports have suggested Paschalides opposes the sale of Vassiliko shares to Cyprus cement, a deal the island's Archbishop apparently favours.
Officials from both companies were not available for comment on Friday. Italy's Italcementi owns 33 percent of Vassiliko.

The CSE index closed at 78.16 on Friday, from 76.05 last week. Banking stocks closed at 87.86 while the manufacturing sector, to which the two cement companies belong, rose to 83.22, gaining 17.1 percent from last week.
Fully paid shares of the Bank of Cyprus gained three cents, closing at 327.5, while the Cyprus Popular Bank gained one cent over the week, closing at 315.
The Hellenic Bank, run by the Hellenic Group, closed at 273.5, gaining seven cents. Group subsidiary Keo, reversed its downward trend of past days and gained eight cents to close at 105.5.
